narrative.overview:
The page is a road. A live three.js scene is fixed behind every page: stepped rice terraces, Mayon's cone with smoke, palms, a nipa hut, kilometre posts on the shoulder and a rider on a motorbike. Scrolling drives the camera down the road and moves the time of day with it, from coral and amber golden hour, through rose and violet dusk, to navy night with stars, fireflies and a yellow headlight. Content does not sit in boxes on top of this world; it rides through it as large type set straight onto the sky.

Two voices carry everything. Anybody, a variable-width face pushed wide (112 to 150 percent), speaks for names, stops, titles and lists that should read as signage. The system sans carries reading text. Colour has strict jobs: pink marks what you can act on (links, selection, the odometer), and yellow is light (the sun, the headlight, the highlighter under the name, and the email address at the close). Text tone flips with the sky: dark ink while the sky is bright, cream once it darkens.

The world rejects the dark-neon developer template and the plain text column it replaced. There are no cards, no glass and no gradient text. Depth comes from the 3D scene and from soft veils of night, not from stacked surfaces.
keyCharacteristics: A fixed 3D world behind every page, with a CSS sky gradient standing in until it is ready.
Time of day as the page's colour system: five sky phases, keyed to sections through `data-sky`.
Wide variable display type set directly on the scene, scaled per stop.
Pink for action, yellow for light, and nothing else saturated in the type layer.
A dashboard HUD: odometer bottom left, pause control bottom right.
Static and fully readable without JavaScript; motion is layered on top and can be paused.

rules.name: The Pink Acts, Yellow Shines Rule
rules.body: Pink is only for things you can act on or that report your position. Yellow is only for light: something lit, highlighted or glowing. Never swap them, and never add a third accent.

rules.name: The Sky Sets The Tone Rule
rules.body: A section's text colour follows its sky phase, not its own choice: phase below 0.5 is day (ink), anything later is night (cream and haze). New sections declare `data-sky` and `data-stop` and inherit the tone.

rules.name: The One Phase Table Rule
rules.body: Sky colours come from the phase table only. Do not hand-pick a background colour for a section.

rules.name: The Heading Steps Back Rule
rules.body: Heading size varies by stop. Where the content is already the headline (the project, the About statement), the stop title drops to the quiet size; where the content is a plain list, the title leads big.

rules.name: The Width Is The Voice Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy in the display face comes from width as much as size: 150 percent for project names, 125 to 140 for stop titles, 100 for anything read as a sentence. Body text never uses the display face.

rules.name: The Veil Not Panel Rule
rules.body: When text needs help against the scene, add a feathered veil of sky or night behind it. Never put text in a box, card or blurred glass panel.

dos: **Do** declare every new section with `data-sky` (a phase from 0 to 4) and `data-stop` (the odometer name), and let tone and sky follow from it.
**Do** set names, stop titles and lists of things in Anybody at 112 to 150 percent width; set sentences in the system sans.
**Do** step the stop title down to the quiet size when the content below it is already the headline.
**Do** keep pink for links, selection and the odometer, and yellow for light, highlights and the contact email.
**Do** use the darker pink (`accent-day`) for any pink text on the day sky.
**Do** help text over the scene with a feathered veil of night or horizon haze.
**Do** keep every page readable with JavaScript off, honour reduced motion with a still frame, and keep the pause control visible whenever anything moves.
donts: **Don't** put content in cards, glass panels or tinted boxes; image frames are the only rounded containers.
**Don't** use gradient text or a third accent colour.
**Don't** pick section backgrounds by hand; the sky comes from the phase table.
**Don't** set body paragraphs in the display face or at a stretched width.
**Don't** add tracked uppercase labels above headings; uppercase tracking belongs to the odometer and the scroll cue only.
**Don't** use light pink (`accent`) text on the day sky; it fails contrast there.
